_comment: Every generated art asset for Sickest Man Alive, with the prompt, reference,
pose and seed that produced it. `tools/generate_art.ps1` reads this (it
forwards to the shared generator in Games/_pipeline/tools). A diff here shows
exactly what changed.
THREE INPUTS, three jobs. Keeping them separate is the whole design:
`pose`   an OpenPose skeleton from tools/make_pose.ps1. Owns the CAMERA
ANGLE and the child proportions. Prompting cannot do this -- a
camera clause loses to the seed every time (proven 2026-08-09).
`ref`    art_ref/kid_concept.png, the character cropped out of the concept
sheet. Owns IDENTITY: the goggle cluster, the orange tank, the
teal-grey suit.
prompt   owns STYLE and detail.
DENOISE means something different once a pose is attached. Without ControlNet
the reference was the only thing holding the anatomy together, so anything
above ~0.5 collapsed the figure -- and 0.45, the one value that worked, sat so
close to the concept art that the sprite was effectively a copy of it. With
the skeleton carrying structure the reference no longer has that job, so
denoise can run high and the result can move away from the concept art without
falling apart. That is the point of the pose input.
SEEDS: `variants` rolls seed, seed+1, ... Never compare two prompts on a
single shared seed. SDXL's composition is dominated by the seed, and a
one-seed comparison measures the seed, not the change under test.
`gen` must be a multiple of 64 -- LayerDiffuse asserts otherwise. The pose PNG
must be generated at the same size, or the joints land somewhere other than
where they were authored.

assets.name: syringe_gun
assets.notes: The concept sheet's own syringe pistol, cropped and background-cleared, passed through the pipeline's trim and cleanup WITHOUT diffusion (generate:false). Regenerating it was not worth the risk: the drawing is already flat cartoon with a hard outline, it is the weapon Richard designed, and SDXL handles a 2.4:1 canvas badly. MUST POINT RIGHT (+X) -- the rig rotates it by the aim angle directly, so a weapon drawn pointing any other way is silently off by that amount.

assets.name: scalpel_sword
assets.notes: As syringe_gun. Also MUST POINT RIGHT (+X), blade away from the grip.

assets.name: enemy_virus
assets.prompt: a single round virus creature, one spherical body covered in short blunt spikes, two angry eyes with small dark pupils, a wide mouth crowded with irregular teeth, sickly acid green, big simple shapes, minimal detail, bold silhouette
assets.negative_extra: swarm, group, many creatures, several, cluster, pair, background sphere, cell, petri dish, arms, legs, limbs
assets.notes: Option A: the spiky sphere from the Virus Swarm concept file. Round, so it reads at any rotation and needs no facing -- the cheapest possible enemy to animate. Enemies draw far smaller than the kid (Enemy.radius is 13), so detail is deliberately starved: at that size a silhouette and two eyes is all that survives. Variant 2 approved 2026-08-09 and copied to art/enemies/virus.png. THE REFERENCE MUST HOLD ONE CREATURE ONLY: an earlier crop caught a second small virus and a speck off to the right, and every generation blended them into a stray appendage growing out of the body.

assets.name: enemy_worm
assets.prompt: a single fat purple grub creature, one humped segmented body, two curved horns on its head, a wide open mouth full of long fangs, small angry eyes, a fringe of short bristles along its underside, dripping slime, big simple shapes, bold silhouette
assets.negative_extra: text, letters, lettering, title, caption, label, logo, graffiti, writing, swarm, group, many creatures, several, cluster, arms, legs, limbs, parchment, paper, book page, anatomy drawing
assets.notes: Option B: the horned grub from the Virus Swarm concept file. Variant 2 approved 2026-08-09 and copied to art/enemies/worm.png. Asymmetric, so it has a front and will need the same left/right turn handling the player has. REPLACED the Bacteria Phalanx blob, which failed three passes -- its reference is a soft low-contrast mass and SDXL returned textured rubble plus invented lettering every time. A subject with an unambiguous silhouette worked first try. Old note on the blob: the Bacteria Phalanx blob. Asymmetric, so it has a front and needs the same left/right turn handling the player has -- more character, more rig. The reference was re-cropped tight to avoid the concept sheet's parchment and anatomy sketch bleeding in.

assets.name: kid
assets.prompt: a small boy in a simple armoured hazmat suit standing facing the viewer, his bare face clearly visible with wide eyes and a worried expression, a pair of round goggle lenses pushed up on his forehead, messy brown hair, one plain orange fluid tank on his back, short and stocky with an oversized head, plain teal-grey armour made of a few large smooth plates, minimal detail, big simple shapes
assets.negative_extra: buckles, straps, pouches, belts, panel lines, rivets, bolts, seams, zips, wires, tubes, clutter, busy surface, intricate detail, fine detail, ornament, greebles, filigree
assets.notes: APPROVED AND LOCKED 2026-08-09. art/kid.png and art_ref/kid.png are both variant 4 of this simplification pass, which itself started from kid_3 of the earlier candidate roll. Richard approved it; do not regenerate over it without asking, because it is now the `ref` for the entire cast and every other character inherits its style through it. denoise 0.45 was deliberately low: this pass had to keep the approved character and only shed surface noise -- a cleanup, not a redesign. The concept sheet is no longer referenced by anything.
